newsitem.title: USA: Pena preps for Energy Dept confirmation hearing.
newsitem.headline: Pena preps for Energy Dept confirmation hearing.

text.p: Energy secretary nominee Federico Pena began a round of briefings Monday to prepare him for his confirmation hearing, possibly to take place in late January, an Energy Department spokeswoman said.

He was due to hold four sessions this week at the Energy Department to begin learning about the agency's four key areas: national security, management and cleanup of nuclear waste, science and technology, and energy resources, said spokeswoman Carmen MacDougall.
"This week is purely introductory," said one official, who declined to be named.
"We were told to prepare briefings as if he doesn't know anything," he said, adding that the instructions would be the same for anyone joining the department.

Senatpr Pete Domenici, a member of the Senate Energy Committee which must recommend the energy nominee to the full Senate, predicted 10 days ago that Pena would "have some trouble being confirmed" because he lacked energy experience.
Pena, who last month resigned as Transportation Secretary, was chosen for the energy job at the last minute as President Clinton sought a Hispanic for his cabinet, according to White House officials.
Clinton said Pena's background managing the Transportation Department, which is as sprawling as the Energy Department, made him a strong nominee.
Pena has not made any announcements about who he might take with him to the Energy Department, a Transportation Department spokesman said.
Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis planned to stay at least until Pena was confirmed, department officials said.
There still was no comment from the Energy Department about senior officials being asked to leave the agency to clear the decks for Pena.

Two weeks ago, administration officials said Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary had told at least three senior women, including assistant secretary for energy efficiency and renewables Christine Ervin, that they should quit.
